title: Analysis By Deep Sequencing of Discontinued Neurotropic Yellow Fever Vaccine Strains.
ehr_evidence: Viruses. Wild-type French viscerotropic (FVV) and Asibi strains were obtained from the World Reference Center for Emerging Viruses and Arboviruses (Galveston, TX, USA) as lyophilized cell culture supernatant.
summary: Deep sequencing and in silico analysis of archived yellow fever vaccine strains (FNV and 17D) and wild-type parental strains to assess genetic diversity, population structure, and reversion to wild-type identity in relation to neurotropic phenotypes.
key_findings: FNV strains showed lower genetic diversity than wild-type FVV, with 19 conserved amino acid substitutions across all four FNV strains.
Eight nucleotide positions were highly unstable, with reversion to wild-type identity most evident in low-neurotropism strains FNV-FC and FNV-NT.
FNV-FC and FNV-NT had higher variant counts (n=131 and n=165) and higher revertant frequencies than high-neurotropism strains FNV-Yale and FNV-IP (n=91 variants each).
17D-204 vaccine diversity was significantly lower than parental Asibi (mean NSE 0.029 vs 0.118, p < 0.001).
Kruskal-Wallis tests showed significant differences in NSE (X2 = 2773.51, df = 6, p < 0.001) and RMSD (X2 = 29970, df = 6, p < 0.001) across all seven strains.
study_design: in vitro genomic sequencing and in silico bioinformatics analysis
population: archived yellow fever virus strains (FNV, 17D-204, Asibi, FVV) from institutional and commercial collections
limitations: passage histories of archived strains are unknown
limited sample size of four FNV strains
neurovirulence data is historical and cited rather than generated in this study
relationship to original Dakar strain is unknown
data_availability_statement: Pre-reduction datasets from sequencing analyses are available from the authors upon request.
